newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Micron Tech downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Micron Tech downgraded.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlack lowered Micron Technology Inc to near-term neutral from accumulate and trimmed the long-term rating to accumulate from buy, a market source said.
-- cut the fiscal fourth quarter earnings estimate to $0.59 a share from $0.70 a share, citing the potential for some margin pressure, the source said.
-- cut the fiscal 1998 earnings estimate to $2.75 a share from $4.05 a share, the source said.
-- Intel Corp's Pentium II is accelerating the market's shift to 64 megabyte chips. The memory market may move to the 64 mb faster than previously anticipated, the source said.

-- Kurlak trimmed the rating on the belief that the 16 megabyte DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chips market may hit its peak momentum in the fourth quarter of this year. A flattening of 16 mb revenues is now expected beginning in calendar first quarter (or fiscal second quarter), the source said.

-- expects sequential revenue decline in Micron's fiscal second quarter as it makes the transition to 64 mb. Fiscal second quarter earnings are expected to drop by 15 percent to $0.56 a share, the source said.
-- does not expect Micron to sustain its 50 percent gross profit margin in memory chips during the transition period.
-- expects pricing for the 64 mb, which is now at $34, to fall 40 to 50 percent in 1998 to the $18-$19 range. The 16 mb should also fall, the source said.
